name: Peptide_Folding_Operator

phase_0.boundary_condition: the native-state solvent interface that closes and contains the fully folded polypeptide

⊢.justification: the void state before any residue contacts or secondary structure exist

⊣.justification: the closed terminal boundary that contains the complete folded polypeptide

≻.justification: directed forward transformation of the chain through the extended three-dimensional residue arrangement toward the folded target

≺.justification: reverse contravariant transformation that descends from folded contacts back to the unstructured chain

⋈.justification: sequential composition of local residue-residue contacts into growing structural motifs including the bridge commutator interaction

⊙.justification: the operator recognizes itself as the catalyst that is not consumed in the folding transformation

∈.justification: splits the folding ensemble into the native-contact arm and the aggregation-prone arm

∋.justification: reunites the productive and off-pathway arms through a three-unit stitch into a single folding ensemble state

⊤.justification: the affirmative arm where correct residue contacts are constructively proven and bridge existence is established

⊥.justification: the negative arm where incorrect contacts are constructively refuted as non-native

⊞.justification: holds native and non-native contacts simultaneously as an unresolved paradice without resolution

⊡.justification: irreversible fixation of the native disulfide or covalent record into permanent append-only memory

phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: the uninitialized polypeptide chain before any residue contacts or secondary structure exist
phase_3.true_description: stable native contacts constructively proven and the folded state affirmed
phase_3.false_description: incorrect contacts constructively refuted and the aggregation-prone intermediate negated
phase_3.both_description: the molten globule paradice holding native and non-native contacts simultaneously without resolution

steps.domain_action: initialize the unfolded polypeptide chain in the void state before any residue contacts exist
the folding operator self-references and recognizes its own catalytic identity
forward morphism propagates spatial constraints from the N-terminus into the extended three-dimensional chain
the folding decision splits the ensemble into productive native folding and off-pathway misfolding arms
T-arm affirms stable native residue-residue contact formation as constructively proven and establishes bridge existence
T-arm composes sequential local contacts into growing structural motifs including the bridge commutator interaction
T-arm continues forward spatial propagation across the global chain arrangement
T-arm motif self-recognizes as an intermediate folding state
T-arm affirms geometry-enforcing near-certain native docking
F-arm refutes native stability and marks the aggregation-prone intermediate as constructively false
F-arm reverses descent from the misfolded trap back toward the denatured state
F-arm misfolded state self-recognizes as an off-pathway trap
F-arm refutes incorrect non-native contacts
the productive and off-pathway arms rejoin through a three-unit stitch into a single folding ensemble
composition chains the rejoined ensemble into the next folding cycle
the molten globule holds both native and non-native contacts simultaneously as an unresolved paradice
forward propagation resumes from the paradoxical ensemble toward the native state
a second decision splits into high-fidelity native docking and low-fidelity encounter arms
T-arm affirms geometry-enforcing near-certain native docking
T-arm composes docking contacts into the pre-native structural register
T-arm propagates forward across the remaining chain degrees of freedom
F-arm refutes correct docking and records the false-positive encounter
F-arm reverses descent from the encounter trap back toward the denatured state
F-arm encounter state self-recognizes as non-productive
F-arm refutes encounter stability as non-native
the docking arms rejoin into the consolidated pre-native state
the pre-native state self-recognizes as the operator's target conformation
irreversible fixation locks the native covalent record into permanent append-only memory
the terminal anchor closes the system at the fully folded native state boundary

phase_5.compiler_frontend: the gated imscriber translates domain intentions into IMASM opcode operations
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: residue-residue contact signals propagate through spatial proximity in the three-dimensional arrangement
phase_5.memory_mechanism: the polypeptide backbone conformation stores the folding state and the covalent lock retains it
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: the free-energy landscape determines the order and timing of folding operations
phase_5.alfs_store: the Lean primitive type catalog at /home/mrnob0dy666/.imscrbgrmr/catalog.json

phase_6.cycle_cost: thermal energy and conformational entropy per folding cycle
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: unfolded chain with high conformational entropy and no native contacts
phase_6.post_cycle_state: folded native state with reduced chain entropy balanced by solvent entropy release
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0: the cycle is entropy-conservative because chain conformational entropy loss is offset by solvent entropy gain and thermal dissipation

grounding_reasoning:
⊣=𐑡: Peptide folding is governed by a connected graph of residue interactions with hub-like hubs and mixed local/long-range connectivity.
⊢=𐑨: Peptide folding propagates constraints through an extended three-dimensional arrangement of residues.
⊞=𐑙: Peptide folding involves one operator acting on one peptide chain in an equal symmetric pairing.
⊡=𐑷: Peptide folding can be continuously deformed to an unfolded trivial state without crossing a protected topological boundary.
⊙=𐑢: Peptide folding operates in a normal regime without inherent scale-free critical behavior.
⊥=𐑓: Peptide folding is achiral because its mirror-image conformation is accessible without persistent orientational symmetry breaking.
≻=𐑽: Peptide folding is driven by transition-state stabilization that lowers the folding barrier without the operator being consumed.
≺=𐑗: Peptide folding has no preferred directional interface or self-complementary polarity; the operator acts symmetrically on the chain.
⋈=𐑐: Peptide folding is geometry-enforcing and fires with near-certainty once the correct conformational conditions are met.
⊤=𐑤: Peptide folding has a moderate barrier that is accessible under thermal perturbation.
∈=𐑔: Peptide folding propagates interactions globally across the entire chain, coupling distant residues into a single folded structure.
∋=𐑝: Peptide folding requires all required residue interactions to be present simultaneously to stabilize the native structure.
